proposition.claim:
Equation reference: eq:E. Section 2.1.2 works in the category \(\mathrm{Ch}^{\mathbb Z}\) of complexes of internally \(\mathbb Z\)-graded abelian groups. Write \(\mathcal D^\mathbb Z\) for its derived category. The polynomial algebra \[\Sigma=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathbb Z(n)=\mathbb Z[t]\] has \(t\) in cohomological degree zero and internal degree \(-1\), with primitive coproduct \(t\mapsto t\otimes1+1\otimes t\). The square-zero differential graded algebra on page 7 is \[
 I=\mathbb Z(-1)[-1],\qquad E=\mathbb Z\oplus I,\qquad I^2=0.\] In cohomological notation its generator \(\epsilon\) has degree \(1\) and internal degree \(1\); all differentials are zero. The source uses the right-induced projective model structure on \(E\)-modules, and a left-induced model structure on \(\Sigma\)-modules whose weak equivalences are the underlying quasi-isomorphisms. Both present the respective usual derived module categories.

The general motivic base \(S\) is connected and smooth of finite type over a Dedekind ring or a field (Notation 2.11). The geometric construction uses a split reductive group and facets in the closure of a fixed alcove. Assertions involving the mixed Tate heart retain the stated Beilinson–Soulé hypothesis, except where reduced motives remove that requirement. Integral motives and rationally defined monodromy are distinguished throughout the review.

The dependency relevant here is specific. Corollary 2.20, whose proof continues on page 12, invokes Lemma 2.9 to identify the reduced Tate category on \(\mathbb G_m\) with \(\operatorname{Nilp}\), and uses rational coefficients for the corresponding unreduced identification. Definition 2.24 then forms the functor with values in \(\operatorname{Nilp}_{\mathbb Q}\operatorname{DTM}(S)\). In the proof of Theorem 3.2, page 16 explicitly forms extension of scalars through this functor. The same foundational construction is repeated in several variables on page 22, and enters the monodromy-compatible convolution construction in Lemma 4.20, page 32. Thus this is an operative step in the paper’s enhanced nearby-cycle construction.

The derived tensor functor of the expressly specified augmentation Sigma-E bimodule Z is fully faithful.
